la:verb:paveo.gloss: to be struck with fear, to be afraid or terrified; tremble or quake with fear
senses: to be struck with fear, to be afraid or terrified; tremble or quake with fear
to fear, dread or be terrified by
la:verb:paveo.html:
păvĕo, pāvi (
part. pres. gen. plur. paventūm, ), 2, v. n. and a. [etym. dub.; perh. akin with pavio].
Neutr., to be struck with fear or terror, to tremble or quake with fear, to be afraid, be terrified (perh. not used by Cic.; not in Cæs.; syn.: tremo, trepido, timeo, metuo): nam et intus paveo et foris formido,: mihi paveo,; : ne pave,; : quaeres, quando iterum paveas,: paventes ad omnia,: repente Maurus incerto vultu pavens ad Sullam accurrit,in great fear,; : admiratione paventibus cunctis,seized with astonishment,; cf.: speque metuque pavent,: in alieno discrimine sibi pavens, ne adlevasse videretur,; cf. venae,: hoc sermone pavent,i. e. express their fears,.—With prepp. (eccl. Lat.): pavete ad sanctuarium meum,; cf. : pavens pro arcā Dei,: pavebit a facie consilii Domini,; cf. ; 31, 4: super quo pavet anima,.—
Act., to fear, dread, be terrified at: et illud paveo et hoc formido,; so with a general object: ad hoc mulieres . . . miserari parvos liberos, rogitare, omnia pavere,: noctem paventes, Poët. ap. : quis Parthum paveat, quis gelidum Scythen?: ut pavet acres Agna lupos capreaeque leones!: tristiorem casum,: mores alicujus,: saturam serpentibus ibin,: mortem,: funera,: (Castanea) pavet novitatem,.—Pass. (in , read batuerentur): nec pedibus tantum pavendas serpentes,.—Perh. here too belongs: paveri frumenta dicebant antiqui, quae de vaginā non bene exibant, Fest. p 251 and 253 Müll.; v. Müll. ad loc.—
With inf. (poet.): pavetque Laedere jactatis maternas ossibus umbras,: nec illae numerare aut exigere plagas pavent,.

la:noun:pavimentum.html:
păvīmentum, i, n.
pavio
,
a floor composed of small stones, earth, or lime, beaten down with a rammer, a hard floor, a pavement: ibi de testā aridā pavimentum struito: ubi structum erit pavito fricatoque oleo, uti pavimentum bonum siet,; so ; : pavimenta Poenica marmore Numidico constrata significat Cato, cum ait, etc., Müll.: facere,: mero Tingere pavimentum,: pavimenta fistucis pavita,; cf. ; .—Also, of the covering of a roof, tiling, Auct. B. Alex. 1.

id.

la:verb:pavito.gloss: to tremble or shake with fear
senses: to tremble or shake with fear
la:verb:pavito.html:
păvĭto, āre,
v. freq. n. and a. [paveo].
In gen., to tremble or quake with fear, to be very fearful, be greatly afraid; to tremble at (ante-class. and poet.): quae pueri in tenebris pavitant,: prosequitur pavitans,: effusis pavitantem fletibus,: pavitante gressu sequere fallaces vias,.—
In partic., to shake or shiver with the ague, to have the ague, .

la:noun:pavor.gloss: The act of trembling, quaking, throbbing or panting with fear.
senses: The act of trembling, quaking, throbbing or panting with fear.
Fear through expectation, dread, thrill, anxiety, trepidation.
la:noun:pavor.html:
păvor (old nom. pavos, Naev. ap. ; Fragm. Trag. 45 Rib.; Pac. ap. ; Fragm. Trag. v. 82 Rib.; B. and K. read pavor), ōris, m.
paveo
,
a trembling, quaking, throbbing, panting with fear, desire, joy, etc., anxiety, fear, dread, alarm, etc. (perh. not used by Cic.; syn.: metus, timor, tremor): pavorem, metum mentem loco moventem; ex quo illud Enni: tum pavor sapientiam omnem mi exanimato expectorat, (this verse of Ennius is also cited in ; cf. also Vahl., and Trag. Rel. p. 17 Rib.): hic exsultat enim pavor ac metus,; : tantus terror pavorque omnes occupavit, ut, etc.,: pavor ceperat milites ne, etc.,: pavorem inicere,: incutere,; : pavorem deponere,: pellere,: lenire,.—Of expectant or joyful trembling: cum spes arrectae juvenum, exsultantiaque haurit Corda pavor pulsans,; : laeto pavore proditus,.—Of religious fear, awe, : pavor aquae,dread of water, hydrophobia,; (in , aquae timor; Gr. ὑδροφοβία).—
Plur.: venia est tantorum danda pavorum,; : contra formidines pavoresque,: repentini,: nocturni,; ; .—
Păvor, personified, the god of fear, ; ; ; v. pallor fin.—His priests are called Pavorii, .

la:adj:pavidus.html:
păvĭdus, a, um, adj.
paveo
,
trembling, quaking, fearful, terrified, alarmed, timid, timorous (perhaps not in Cic.).
Lit.: timida atque pavida,; : castris se pavidus tenebat,: matres,: miles,: pavidus semper atque anxius,: lepus,: aves,: pavida ex somno mulier,startled out of her sleep,: ad omnes suspiciones pavidus,: oppidani pavidi, ne jam facta in urbem via esset, fossam ducere instituunt,.—Comp.: quos pavidiores accepimus, .—Sup.: intra mens pavidissima,; .—
With gen.: nandi pavidus,: offensionum non pavidus,: maris,: lucis,: leti,.—
With inf. (poet.): Carthalo non pavidus fetas mulcere leaenas,.—
In neutr. adverbially: pavidum blandita,with fear, timorously,.—
Transf.
Accompanied with fear or anxiety, anxious, disturbed: pavidum murmur,: furtum,: fuga,: quies pavida imaginibus,. —
That produces fear, fearful, terrible, dreadful: metus,: lucus,.—Adv.: păvĭdē, with fear, fearfully, timorously (rare): timefactae religiones effugiunt animo pavide,: fugere,: dicere,.

la:verb:pavesco.html:
păvesco, ĕre,
v. inch. n. and a. [paveo] (mostly post-Aug.).
Neutr., to begin to be afraid, to become alarmed: omni strepitu pavescere,: ad ejusmodi tactum,: ad nocturnas imagines, (al. expavescere): pavescere sensim et quasi albescere,.—
Act., to begin to fear or dread, to begin to be alarmed at: bellum,: prodigia deūm,.

la:verb:pavio.html:
păvĭo, īvi, ītum, 4, v. a.
kindr. with παιω
,
to beat, strike.
Lit.: pavit aequor harenam,: aliquid ex ore pavire terram,.—
Transf., to beat, ram, or tread down: aream esse oportet solidam, terrā pavitā,: sato pavitur terra,: pavimenta fistucis pavita,: pavitum solum,.—Hence, păvītum, i, n., a hard-beaten floor, a pavement (post-class.), .
